seoTitle: Place Buy and Sell Trades on TradingView
metaDescription: Learn how to place a trade on TradingView using the trading panel, set order type and quantity, and modify stop loss or take profit afterward.
intro: Placing trades directly from TradingView's charting interface is straightforward once you know where the trading panel and order options live. This guide covers opening a new order, setting your parameters, and modifying an existing trade's stop loss and take profit.

steps.heading: Open the trading panel
steps.body: Locate the trading panel at the bottom of the TradingView interface to see available brokers and trading setups.

steps.heading: Connect to paper or live trading
steps.body: Use paper trading to practice risk-free, or connect to your live broker if you're ready to trade with real funds.

steps.heading: Open a new order ticket
steps.body: Click the trade button and select the order option to start configuring your trade.

steps.heading: Set order type and quantity
steps.body: Choose between a market or limit order and specify the asset and quantity you want to trade.

steps.heading: Confirm and execute
steps.body: Double-check your order details before confirming to execute the trade.

steps.heading: Modify stop loss and take profit
steps.body: Use the modify order option to adjust SL and TP levels on an existing trade as market conditions change.

faq.question: Where do I place a trade on TradingView?
faq.answer: You place trades through the trading panel at the bottom of the interface, using the trade button to open a new order.

faq.question: Can I practice trades without risking money?
faq.answer: Yes, paper trading lets you place simulated trades without financial risk before going live.

faq.question: What order types can I use?
faq.answer: You can choose between market and limit orders when configuring a trade.

faq.question: Can I change stop loss or take profit after placing a trade?
faq.answer: Yes, the modify order option lets you adjust SL and TP levels on an existing trade.

faq.question: Do I need a connected broker to place trades?
faq.answer: For live trading you need a connected broker, but paper trading works without one.
